title: Controlled dummy SWAP - Ribasim - MODFLOW conflict triangle
purpose: Compose the qualified-shape one-Basin oracle with minimal transactional dummy SWAP demand and dummy MODFLOW forecast/realization participants, so water-allocation conflicts can be isolated without production physics.

swap: publishes irrigation demand from committed state only
does not recalculate same-window demand from tentative Ribasim or MODFLOW state
records realized delivery and shortage only on explicit coupled commit
modflow: publishes forecast Basin infiltration/drainage for allocation
publishes actual Basin infiltration/drainage for physical realization
does not clip actual physical exchange to satisfy UserDemand
records the realized exchange only on explicit coupled commit
ribasim: allocates from committed Basin state and MODFLOW forecast
realizes actual physical exchange before managed delivery
curtails managed UserDemand when actual hydrology leaves less allocatable water
fails closed if actual mandatory infiltration would require negative Basin storage

transaction_contract: commit preflights all participant revisions before mutating any participant
stale candidates fail closed with zero participant mutation
one successful coupled commit advances all three participant revisions exactly once

experiments.C1: forecast equals actual: requested irrigation is fully allocated and delivered; all participants commit once
experiments.C2: late conflict: SWAP requests 50 m3, MODFLOW forecast permits 50 m3 allocation, actual infiltration leaves only 40 m3, Ribasim delivers 40 m3 and SWAP records 10 m3 shortage
experiments.C3: forecast already reveals shortage: allocation shortage is distinguished from later realization shortage
experiments.C4: actual hydrology infeasible: coupled prepare fails with zero mutation of SWAP, Ribasim and MODFLOW
experiments.C5: stale coupled candidate after independent participant advancement fails before any coupled mutation
experiments.C6: same-window SWAP request is invariant to tentative allocation/realization; no hidden feedback from candidate delivery into demand

forbidden: no SWAP production hydrology or irrigation physics
no Ribasim network-routing or allocation-equivalence claim
no same-window demand iteration unless separately preregistered
